docker/compose: 36 oracle cross-references on files fathom does not read were left out of scope (§1.4)
per-file times exclude the one-time grammar compile (an untimed warm-up extraction precedes timing)
disposition: partial: L1 and L2 excellent against a tier-A oracle (docker compose config --format json v5.1.4, run with --no-normalize so inferred dependencies stay out) across docker/awesome-compose and docker/compose's pkg/e2e/fixtures (145 files): sym_recall 1.0, sym_precision .9962 (264/265; the one dialect-only service is the deliberately invalid wrong-composefile fixture the tool rejects), ref_recall/ref_precision 1.0 (43/43 depends_on pairs). L3 not attempted: the tier-C xref oracle finds 36 cross-file edges over the two subjects and none is scorable — 35 are build: context/dockerfile edges onto Dockerfiles (files a doc-engine dialect never reads, dropped as out of scope, section 1.4) and the one extends.file edge lands on common.yaml, a fragment no compose name rule claims. Nor could the resolver join them: fusion.ResolveDocXrefs resolves a repo-path reference to the target file's root entity and a compose file has none (top-level name: is optional; the engine has no file-name value), and a Dockerfile is a tags-engine file outside the doc-xref index (LB-X-docker-image-ref). extends.file and include are recorded in DocResult.CrossFile so they resolve once a root entity exists. Trigger: the doc engine gains a file-name value and content-based ownership of arbitrarily named compose fragments, and LB-X-docker-image-ref lands; then this reading is re-measured on a subject that uses extends.file or include.
